issues.legal_issue: Unreliable and untrustworthy evidence does not establish an attempted murder charge.
material_facts: The prosecution alleged that the accused fired at a person who escaped injury and that a later shot also missed him.
The accounts of the incident were found unreliable, including because the witnesses’ evidence was inconsistent and did not credibly establish who fired the shots.
issues.conclusion: The convictions for attempted murder were set aside, and both accused were acquitted of those charges.
issues.legal_principle: The prosecution must establish the charge through trustworthy evidence. Applying that principle to the charges under Sections 307/34 of the Indian Penal Code, the Court found the evidence concerning the alleged attack unreliable. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.attempted_assault_testimony_unreliable: The witnesses’ accounts of the alleged attempted assault are not trustworthy.
predicates.accounts_of_attempted_assault_inconsiste: The evidence about how the alleged attempted assault occurred is inconsistent.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal concerns an alleged attempted assault and the testimony is unreliable and inconsistent, the attempted murder charge is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A person charged with murder in furtherance of a common intention is not shown to share that intention where the evidence does not establish that person’s participation in the fatal attack.
material_facts: The fatal shot was attributed to one accused.
The other accused was not shown to have performed an overt act toward committing the murder.
The Court applied the same reasoning by which the acquittal of the other co-accused had been maintained.
issues.conclusion: The accused who was not shown to have participated in the fatal attack was acquitted of the murder charge under Section 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the common-intention charge under Section 302/34 of the Indian Penal Code and concluded, on the evidence in this case, that the accused who had done no overt act toward the murder could not be held liable for it. The judgment cites no earlier cases for this issue.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.fatal_act_attributed_to_another: The evidence attributes the act causing death to another accused.
predicates.no_overt_participation_in_fatal_attack: The accused is not shown to have performed an overt act toward the fatal attack.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a murder conviction, the fatal act is attributed to another person, and the accused is not shown to have participated overtly in the fatal attack, the common-intention murder charge is not established.

issues.legal_issue: A dying declaration identifying the person who caused a fatal injury does not, by itself, negate a raised plea of private defence.
material_facts: The deceased’s statement identified one accused as the person who had fatally injured him.
The accused raised a plea of private defence of person and property.
The declaration was recorded in a crowded room where people were speaking to the deceased and one another, after the deceased had received an injection.
issues.conclusion: The dying declaration could identify the author of the fatal injury, but it did not by itself overcome the plea of private defence or establish the murder charge.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the dying declaration as evidence identifying the person who caused the injury, but held that it was not, by itself, a factor that displaced the accused’s plea of private defence. The judgment cites no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this evidentiary conclusion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a criminal conviction.
predicates.dying_declaration_identifies_shooter: The deceased’s statement identifies a person as the one who caused the fatal injury.
predicates.accused_raises_private_defence: The accused claims to have acted in defence of person or property.

issues.definition: When a criminal appeal involves a dying declaration identifying the assailant and the accused raises private defence, the declaration alone does not negate that defence.

issues.legal_issue: The presence of injuries on an accused and a family member does not, without support from the surrounding circumstances, establish a claim of private defence.
material_facts: The accused and another family member had pellet injuries, and the family member also had simple injuries.
The family member’s injuries were superficial, and the accused were not shown to have surrendered themselves at the time those injuries were allegedly inflicted.
The accused were arrested and medically examined weeks after the occurrence, while the family member was examined several days after it.
The Court found that the injuries alone did not make the defence probable in the circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The injuries on the accused and their family member, standing alone, did not establish or make probable the plea of private defence.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the nature, timing, and surrounding circumstances of the injuries, and held that the mere presence of injuries was insufficient to make the defence probable in this case. The judgment cites no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for this conclusion.

predicates.accused_or_family_member_injured: The accused or a member of the accused’s family had injuries associated with the occurrence.

predicates.injury_circumstances_do_not_corrobate_de: The nature or timing of the injuries and the surrounding conduct do not support the claimed defensive account.

issues.definition: When injuries are the sole support for private defence and their circumstances do not corroborate that defence, the injuries alone do not establish it.

issues.legal_issue: A fatal act may be treated as an exercise of private defence where a confrontation creates a possible apprehension of danger and the accused responds with a single, unrepeated shot.
material_facts: Members of a rival faction had assembled near the accused’s home after an earlier incident, and the Court found it difficult to believe they had come unarmed or without cause.
A direct confrontation occurred between the accused and the assembled group.
The Court considered it possible that the accused apprehended danger to himself and his family.
The accused fired once and did not repeat the shot or fire indiscriminately.
issues.conclusion: The fatal act was treated as an exercise of the right of private defence, and the accused was acquitted of the murder charge.
issues.legal_principle: The Court concluded from the possibility of danger in the confrontation and the accused’s limited response that he acted in private defence of person. The judgment sets aside the murder conviction under Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code; it cites no earlier cases or specific statutory provision for the private-defence conclusion.

predicates.criminal_appeal_from_murder_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal from a murder conviction.
predicates.direct_confrontation: The accused faced a direct confrontation with an assembled group.
predicates.possible_apprehension_of_danger: The circumstances make it possible that the accused apprehended danger to himself or family members.
predicates.single_unrepeated_shot: The accused fired one shot and did not repeat it.

issues.definition: When a murder appeal concerns a direct confrontation, a possible apprehension of danger, and one unrepeated shot, the fatal act falls within private defence.
